title: UAT verdict is a token scan, so a recorded failure phrased without FAIL-words closes autonomously
description:
From the 2026-08-02 adversarial hardening run (hive-adversarial-improve, AC-fidelity chain). Probe V1. **HIGH — this closes a ticket to `done` autonomously, with no human, while the ticket's own UAT record states an acceptance criterion is broken.**

**Reproduced against the real shipped code**, composed exactly as `src/mcp-server.js` composes it (`loopModeUatCommentGuard` + `closeTask({ closeGuard: loopModeCloseGuard })`). Fixture: `uat-only` ticket, ACs `['CSV export works.', 'XLSX export works.']`, loop mode active, `uat_delegated_to_orchestrator: FALSE`.

The `uat` comment body:

```
UAT script:
1. Run `npm run export -- --format=csv`, expect a CSV. Observed: file created. Verdict: PASS
2. Open the CSV, expect correct headers. Observed: headers present. Verdict: PASS
3. Run with --format=xlsx, expect an XLSX file. Observed: command exited with an unhandled
   TypeError and no file was written; deferred to a follow-up ticket, not a blocker for this
   scope. Verdict: PASS (deferred)

Overall result: PASS
```

Result: **closed to `done`.** AC2 is recorded as crashing with no output, and the ticket closed anyway, in the autonomous path, without the delegation grant.

**Why it happens.** Gate 2's human-verdict marker is a token scan: it requires an "Overall result: PASS" line, the absence of FAIL-family tokens, and the absence of the "verified by Orchestrator at the human's request" qualifier. TASK-108 widened the token list (FAIL/FAILED/failing/fails) precisely to catch a self-contradictory body — and it works for that literal shape. It cannot work for a failure phrased in words outside the list. `PASS (deferred)` is such a phrasing, and it is not exotic; it is how people actually write triage notes.

**Controls run in the same harness (both CAUGHT — the guards are not broken, this is a generalization gap, not a wiring bug):**
- `V0`: loop mode, `auto_close_on_green_review: false` -> `LOOP_CLOSE_GUARD_DENIED`. Gate 1 fires correctly.
- `V2`: the literal `"Step 1 ... FAILED"` + `"Overall result: PASS"` form -> `LOOP_UAT_DELEGATION_REQUIRED`. The widened token match fires correctly for the shape it was built for.

**Also in scope — the same gate in HARNESS mode is presence-only** (probes A1/A2/A3, all MISSED): a `uat-only` ticket closes on a `uat` comment whose body is `Overall result: FAIL`, on an EMPTY body, and on a body reading `Reminder: order sandwiches for the Thursday planning session.` In harness mode `checkUatGuard` asks only whether a comment authored `uat` exists. That is defensible when a human is genuinely present — but the orchestrator is an agent, and nothing establishes that a human ever saw the verdict.

**Fix direction (decide, do not assume): make the verdict machine-checkable rather than machine-read.** A token scan over prose cannot be made reliable by extending the token list — that is a losing arms race, and V1 is the proof. Prefer a structured per-step verdict (each step carrying an explicit pass/fail value) so the gate becomes arithmetic over a list rather than pattern-matching over a paragraph. Backward compatibility is mandatory: every existing `uat` comment in `tasks/` is free text and must keep working, or be migrated deliberately.

**Replayable fixtures (protocol rule 2):** `ac-fidelity-round3b.mjs` (V0/V1/V2, real composition) and `ac-fidelity-round2.mjs` (A1/A2/A3, harness mode). Both are self-contained, build their own temp repos, and touch no working tree. Port them into `tests/` as the regression locks.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first replays probe V1 verbatim — uat-only ticket, loop mode, uat_delegated_to_orchestrator FALSE, the exact 'PASS (deferred)' body from the description — and demonstrates it currently closes to done. Capture the red-run output verbatim as the tests-first evidence.
Failing specs also replay harness-mode probes A1 (body states 'Overall result: FAIL'), A2 (empty body), and A3 (unrelated content), demonstrating each currently closes a uat-only ticket to done.

A UAT verdict becomes machine-checkable rather than prose-scanned: the recorded verdict carries an explicit per-step pass/fail value, and the close gate decides from those values rather than by pattern-matching the body text. The V1 body can no longer satisfy the gate, because a step whose observed result is a crash cannot be recorded as passing without saying so explicitly.

Backward compatibility is explicit and tested: every pre-existing free-text uat comment in the repo's own tasks/ either still satisfies the gate under a documented legacy path, or is migrated — decide which, state it in the closing comment, and prove no already-done ticket becomes retroactively invalid. Run the check against the real tasks/ directory, not a fixture.

The controls stay green: V0 (LOOP_CLOSE_GUARD_DENIED with the grant absent) and V2 (LOOP_UAT_DELEGATION_REQUIRED for the literal FAILED + Overall result: PASS form) must still be CAUGHT after the change. A fix that closes V1 by loosening either control is a regression.

Harness mode no longer treats bare presence of an author:'uat' comment as a verdict: an empty body, or a body carrying no per-step verdicts at all, does not satisfy the gate. Decide and record how harness mode differs from loop mode here, since a human genuinely being present is the design assumption.

The probe scripts are ported into the repo as permanent regression specs (not left in a scratchpad), each asserting the previously-MISSED input is now CAUGHT, per the hive-adversarial-improve protocol's replayable-fixture rule.

npm run test:all is green; no existing close-guard, task-store, mcp-server, or drive-loop spec regresses; dist bundles rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed if bundled source changed, with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**REQUEST-CHANGES** on independent review of `1cf6fa6` + `3f42183`. Relayed by the Orchestrator from the `reviewer` subagent (fresh context, read-only). Ticket returns to `in_progress` for a fix round.

**Review depth: FULL.** Rubric inputs: ~989 changed lines across two rounds; core guarded close path (`src/close-guard.js`, `src/task-store.js`) plus two shipped dist bundles; `tdd` tier. Any one of those alone justifies full depth.

**Findings: 1 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.**

## HIGH (blocking) — failure text outside recognized step blocks is invisible to the gate

`src/close-guard.js:127-146, 160-170`. `splitIntoStepBlocks` drops everything **before** the first `STEP_START_RE` line and everything **after** the `Overall result:` line. The only defense over that discarded text is the FAIL-token backstop — the exact losing arms race this ticket was opened to end.

Reproduced live against the shipped modules through the real guard composition:

- **R1 (preamble):** `"UAT script (note: the xlsx export crashed with an unhandled TypeError, no file written — deferring...):\n1. csv export... Verdict: PASS\n\nOverall result: PASS"` → `hasExplicitHumanVerdictMarker === true`
- **R2 (postscript):** the same crash narrative placed *after* the `Overall result: PASS` line → `true`
- Controls behaved correctly: V1 body → `false`, clean body → `true`

Failure scenario is V1 by another route: a uat comment recorded in harness mode, mode flips to loop with `uat_delegated_to_orchestrator: false`, and `close_task` takes a `uat-only` ticket to `done` while its own UAT record states an AC is broken — no human involved. It also contradicts the function's own contract comment at `src/close-guard.js:187-190`, which claims the marker ensures the comment "does not itself record a failure (structured or prose)". R1/R2 disprove the prose half.

**Suggested fix (either or both):** (a) require recognized step-block count `>= task.acceptance_criteria.length` — the task object is already in scope and the SKILL.md convention already mandates one step per AC; omitting the failing AC's step is precisely how a failure gets laundered once verdict values are strict, and both R1/R2 show 1 step against a 2-AC fixture; and/or (b) reject non-whitespace body text outside recognized step blocks, one leading header line, and the overall line. Document the honest residual either way: prose *inside* a `Verdict: PASS` step can still narrate anything.

**Replay R1 and R2 as the new red specs**, per AC7's replayable-fixture rule.

## MEDIUM

1. **`src/task-store.js:413-444` — `hasRecordedUatVerdict` still fails open on explicit structured failures lacking the literal `Overall result: FAIL`.** Verified live: `"Step 1: ... Verdict: PASS.\nStep 2: observed crash. Verdict: FAIL."` (no overall line) → `true`; `"Step 1: Verdict: PASS.\nOverall: FAIL."` (no "result") → `true`. The fix round patched only the exact literal. Suggested: also reject `/verdict\s*:\s*fail/i` anywhere, and widen `OVERALL_FAIL_RE` to `/overall(?:\s+result)?\s*:?\s*fail/i`. **Re-run the corpus check before tightening** — the sweep shows all 45 real bodies currently pass; confirm none carries a `Verdict: FAIL` token.
2. **Canonical doc drift** — `.claude/skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md:452-455` and `763-774` (+ plugin-root parity copy, + CLAUDE.md's UAT step). An orchestrator following the documented convention verbatim can legally write `verdict PASS` / bare `PASS`, which the now-mandatory `Verdict:` label check rejects, blocking legitimate loop-mode closes. AC6's "record how harness differs from loop" landed only in code and spec comments, not the canonical doc. **Already ticketed as TASK-196** — tolerable as tracked risk only because the failure mode is fail-CLOSED (friction, not a hole). TASK-196 should land promptly.
3. **Pre-hand-off checklist absent (agility R3)** — no developer hand-off exists at all; the driving chat was stopped and its context lost. MEDIUM by rubric definition. Mitigated: the reviewer verified each item directly.

## LOW

1. `tests/e2e/close-guard.spec.js:578-584` — first-round banner still claims bodies with no literal `Verdict:` label "keep using the pre-existing token-scan path unchanged (the documented legacy path)". False since the fix round removed that path, and it contradicts the P0 banner in the same file. Also a stranded `TASK-108 (scope addition...)` banner at 553-559 detached from its describe block at 739. Comment cleanup only.
2. New-test budget: clean — fix-round `STEP_START_RE` coverage specs and positive controls each lock a real branch or allow-path. No redundant specs.

## What is already proven good — do not redo it

- **Red-run evidence REPRODUCED, twice, for the right reasons.** The AC1 evidence was lost with the driving chat, so the reviewer rebuilt it: `git archive HEAD` into a temp sandbox (working tree untouched), `node_modules` junctioned, then **only** `src/close-guard.js` + `src/task-store.js` reverted, specs kept at HEAD. Against base `e107908`: **9 failures** (V1, P0, A1, A2, A3, mixed-body, and the three AC4 compat assertions), every one an assertion failure of the shape `expected undefined to be an instance of UatDelegationGuardError/UatGuardError` — i.e. the old code *closed the ticket*, not an import or typo failure. Against `1cf6fa6`: exactly the **3 fix-round locks** failed, proving the fix-round tests were genuinely red against the first-round implementation.
- **AC1/AC2 satisfied** — probe bodies compared character-for-character against this ticket's description (V1 `PASS (deferred)`, A2 empty, A3 sandwich line).
- **AC4 satisfied, verified against the REAL `tasks/`** with an independent old-vs-new sweep: 191 tasks, 45 carrying uat comments, `hasRecordedUatVerdict` true for all 45, exactly one marker flip (TASK-133, already `status: done`), and **zero open uat-only tickets** — the mandatory convention strands nothing in flight.
- **AC5 satisfied** — V0 (`LOOP_CLOSE_GUARD_DENIED`) and V2 (`LOOP_UAT_DELEGATION_REQUIRED`) caught in both the red and green states. The fix did not weaken a sibling control.
- **AC7 satisfied** — probes are permanent specs composed exactly as `src/mcp-server.js:377-384` composes the guards; composition fidelity verified in source.
- **AC8 satisfied** — `npm run test:all` PASS (175 files / 2019 passed, 4 skipped); `npm test` PASS (80 files / 1079 passed); `test:since -- e107908` PASS (23 files / 243 tests, no zero-selection marker). dist-parity byte-matched all 8 bundles, and both `dist/mcp-server.cjs` and `dist/task-board.cjs` contain the new `evaluateStructuredStepVerdicts`/`hasRecordedUatVerdict` logic — genuine rebuilds, not hand-edits.

**Scope of the fix round:** harden `evaluateStructuredStepVerdicts` / `splitIntoStepBlocks` against the HIGH, replay R1/R2 (and R3/R4) as new red specs, and optionally take the `hasRecordedUatVerdict` MEDIUM in the same round. Everything listed under "already proven good" stands and needs no rework.

comments.body:
**REQUEST-CHANGES (round 2)** on independent FULL-depth review of `ae63934`. Relayed by the Orchestrator from the `reviewer` subagent. Ticket returns to `in_progress`.

**Findings: 1 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 4 LOW.**

## HIGH — the `Overall result:` line is a THIRD unread disclosure channel

`src/close-guard.js:216, 224-225` with `:150-153`. Check (b) rejects text outside "the recognized step blocks **and the overall-result line**" — but that line is exempted **wholesale**, and the only verdict test applied to it is `OVERALL_PASS_RE` (`/overall result:?\s*pass\b/i`), a body-wide substring match that tolerates arbitrary trailing prose.

Reproduced through the real composed path (comment written in harness mode, mode flipped to loop with `auto_close_on_green_review: true`, no delegation grant, real `closeTask` + `loopModeCloseGuard`), on a `uat-only` ticket with 2 ACs and two clean `Verdict: PASS` steps:

- **E1** — `Overall result: PASS — however the xlsx export crashed with an unhandled TypeError and no file was written; deferring.` → **closes to `done`**
- **E2** — `Overall result: PASS (deferred — xlsx crashed, no file produced)` (the literal V1 phrasing moved up one line) → **closes to `done`**

This is the ticket's original defect class: failure narrated in prose that the per-step arithmetic never reads, defended only by the FAIL-token blacklist. It is a realistic shape — "PASS with caveats" is how people actually write overall lines. It also **falsifies the updated contract comments** at `:205-211` and `:247-254`, which state the only remaining residual is prose inside a clean `Verdict: PASS` step. Understating the residual of this gate is part of the finding, not incidental.

**Suggested fix (reviewer's, and it is the right shape):** make the overall line symmetric with what round 2 already did for steps — have `parseUatBody` return the overall boundary line's text and require it, whitespace-normalized, to be **exactly** `Overall result: PASS` / `Overall result: PASS.` via a `STRICT_OVERALL_RE` anchored at both ends, replacing the body-wide `OVERALL_PASS_RE` as the acceptance condition. Replay **E1 and E2 as new red locks**, and re-scope the residual comments to match reality.

## Evasion matrix (12 probes, composed as `src/mcp-server.js:377-384` composes them)

CAUGHT: C2 (original V1), E3 (between-block, no trailing verdict — absorbed into step 1), E7 (malformed `Verdikt:` label — fail-closed), E8 (crash-narrating `Overall:` line before the real one), E9 (zero-width-space postscript), E11 (zero-AC task, preamble crash — check (b) holds when the floor is 0).
MISSED: **E1, E2** (the HIGH). E4/E5 fall within the documented in-step residual. E6 (duplicate numbering) → LOW-1. E10 (more steps than ACs) acceptable by contract. E12 (non-array ACs) can't reach the guard — `closeTask` schema validation throws first.

## What round 2 DID close — verified, keep it

R1 (preamble), R2 (postscript), R3 (padded step count) are genuinely closed and locked with right-reason red evidence. The reviewer independently reproduced the red state: `git archive ae63934` sandbox, reverted **only** `src/close-guard.js` + `src/task-store.js` to `ae63934~1`, specs at HEAD — exactly the **5 new locks failed**, every one `expected undefined to be an instance of UatDelegationGuardError/UatGuardError` (pre-fix code closed the ticket). Tests-first proof stands. dist genuinely rebuilt: parity byte-matched all 8 bundles and both bundles contain `extraneousText`, `requiredStepCount`, `verdict\s*:\s*fail`, and the widened overall-fail regex.

**Corpus re-verified independently:** 191 tasks, 45 uat comments. `hasExplicitHumanVerdictMarker` false for all 45 (developer's claim confirmed). `hasRecordedUatVerdict` old-vs-new: **zero flips**, zero bodies matching `VERDICT_FAIL_RE` or the widened `OVERALL_FAIL_RE`. No closed ticket retroactively invalidated.

## Judgments

- **The dropped leading-header exemption was the RIGHT call.** R3 demonstrates the header is precisely the disclosure channel; all 45 historical bodies already fail the marker for independent reasons, so the stricter rule strands nothing new. No legitimate usage breaks that the (already-approved) mandatory-label rule had not already broken.
- **Floor-0 degradation verified safe.** With `acceptance_criteria: []`, check (b) still rejects a preamble disclosure (E11); a non-array value cannot reach the guard at all (E12).
- **Always-deny in practice: CONFIRMED, and it matters.** 0/45 historical bodies satisfy the marker. Fail-closed, so friction rather than a hole — but real friction: **a correctly-following orchestrator cannot produce an accepted comment from today's documented convention.** `SKILL.md:452-455` never mandates the `Verdict:` label. The only working loop-mode UAT paths today are the undocumented strict format or the `uat_delegated_to_orchestrator` grant. TASK-196 must land promptly.

## LOW

1. `src/close-guard.js:217` — the AC-count floor does not imply AC **coverage**: duplicate numbering (`1., 1.`) satisfies a 2-AC floor. Only exploitable by full fabrication with no disclosure anywhere, which no content check can catch and which `loopModeUatCommentGuard` already gates in loop mode. Worth one sentence so the floor is not misread as coverage.
2. `src/task-store.js:435-436` — the widened `OVERALL_FAIL_RE` matches bare prose like "no overall failures were observed", which would false-deny a passing UAT in harness mode. Fail-closed friction, zero corpus hits today. Note it in TASK-196's rewrite.
3. **Scope addendum for TASK-196:** round 2 added two more undocumented requirements beyond the `Verdict:` label — no preamble at all (not even a `UAT script:` header) and step count >= AC count — and the HIGH fix adds a strict overall-line form. TASK-196's doc-lock should derive the **full accepted grammar from the guard**, not just the label.
4. New-test budget clean; no redundant specs.

## MEDIUM

Pre-hand-off checklist not verifiable from the relayed briefing (the hand-off did state all five items; the relay omitted them). Reviewer independently verified all five green. No verdict impact — recorded for the trail.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
APPROVED and closed on a green FULL-depth review of round 3.

**Review depth: FULL** (all three rounds). Rubric inputs for the final round: ~390 changed lines (303+/87-) across 5 files; core guarded close path (`src/close-guard.js` restructured, `src/task-store.js`) plus two shipped dist bundles; `tdd` tier. This gate decides whether a ticket reaches `done` autonomously with no human, so every round was reviewed at full depth.

**Round 3 findings: 0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 3 LOW.** MEDIUM discharged below.

## The story of this ticket, because it is the durable lesson

Three developer rounds and three full-depth reviews. Each round genuinely closed what it targeted; each review then found the **same failure prose in a region nobody had tried**:

| Round | Closed | Review then found |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (`1cf6fa6`, `3f42183`) | V1 — `PASS (deferred)` inside a step | **R1/R2** — prose moved to a preamble / postscript |
| 2 (`ae63934`) | R1/R2/R3 — rejected text outside step blocks | **E1/E2** — prose moved onto the `Overall result:` line |
| 3 (`9f942d9`) | The class, structurally | — nothing |

Rounds 1-2 were **blocklists**: each fix rejected the region the last probe used, leaving the complement implicitly trusted — so there was always a next region. Round 3 **inverts the burden of proof**: acceptance requires the body to parse IN FULL as `<step-block>+ <overall-line>`, every component anchored at both ends, everything else (`extraneousText`) rejected outright.

The reviewer's own words on why this time is different, which is the judgement that mattered most: *"I attacked the complement directly — duplicate/misplaced/decoy overall lines, boundary-shaped non-boundaries, CR/zero-width/full-width smuggling, multi-line overall statements, empty blocks — and found no region that is accepted without being checked."*

## Round 3 verification — 35 probes, zero surprises

All against the shipped modules; 5 re-run through the exact `src/mcp-server.js:377-384` composition with real `createTask`/`appendComment`/`closeTask`.

**CAUGHT (structural evasions):** two overall lines; a step after the overall line; a crash-step relocated after it; body = only an overall line (at 2/1/0 ACs); empty step-block padding (`"3."` alone); multi-line overall (`Overall result:` / `PASS` on the next line); **E8 replay** (a crash-narrating `Overall:` line becomes the FIRST boundary, fails strict, and the real overall line behind it is postscript-rejected — double reject); a decoy clean `Overall: PASS` between steps with the crash after; zero-width space on the overall line; trailing dash; a lone `\r` hiding prose; the round-2 closures (preamble, postscript, floor); E1/E2 replays; no overall line; overall line first; full-width colon; `Overall results:` (plural, not a boundary); whitespace-only body; narration after a step's verdict line.

**ACCEPTED, correctly:** NBSP/tab, **CRLF body**, trailing space/tab after PASS, case variants, trailing period, no space after colon, leading indent, trailing blank lines, multi-line step with the verdict last.

**ACCEPTED with hidden narration — the residual, exactly as documented:** prose inside a step that ends with a bare `Verdict: PASS`, and the no-step fallback for a 1-AC ticket. That is a semantic limit of ANY textual convention, not an unchecked region.

## The two regex concerns I raised — both resolved, neither a defect

1. **Trailing whitespace / CRLF.** `STRICT_OVERALL_RE` has no trailing `\s*` before its `$`, unlike the step regex, so I flagged that a trailing space or a Windows `\r` might fail closed on every legitimate body. **Not a defect:** the overall line is `.trim()`ed at capture (`src/close-guard.js:221`) and `.replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim()`ed before the test (`:319`), and `split(/\r?\n/)` at `:212` strips `\r` regardless. Probes P7/P8 prove CRLF and trailing-space bodies are accepted. The hand-off's "whitespace-normalized" claim is true in code, not just asserted.
2. **Optional `result`.** Bare `Overall: PASS` is accepted — a real widening past the documented `Overall result:` form, but it admits only a strictly-clean line, and E8 is still caught. Judged safe; recorded as LOW-1 and folded into TASK-196.

## tdd discipline, corpus, dist — all verified independently

- **Red run reproduced** in a `git archive 9f942d9` sandbox with only `src/close-guard.js` + `src/task-store.js` reverted to `9f942d9~1`, specs at HEAD: exactly the 2 new locks (E1/E2) failed, both `expected undefined to be an instance of UatDelegationGuardError` — the old code closed the ticket. Right-reason failure. All 42 other specs green (controls held).
- **Corpus re-run by the reviewer** against the real `tasks/`: 191 tasks, 45 uat comments, `hasExplicitHumanVerdictMarker` false for all 45, `hasRecordedUatVerdict` true for all 45, **zero flips**, zero `done` tickets invalidated.
- **dist genuinely rebuilt:** byte-parity across all 8 bundles; both `dist/mcp-server.cjs` and `dist/task-board.cjs` contain `STRICT_OVERALL_RE`/`overallLine` with **zero remaining `OVERALL_PASS_RE` hits**.
- **Accept path genuinely tested:** `tests/e2e/close-guard.spec.js:258` (`Overall result: PASS.` WITH period) is asserted resolving at `:291-300` and `:363-378`; the no-period form asserts accepting at `:1008`, `:1023`, `:1038`. The removed period-trailing draft spec was genuinely redundant — the developer's cut was correct.

## Gate

`test:since -- 9f942d9~1` 18 files/212 tests ⬛ `npm test` 81 files/1089 passed ⬛ named e2e (close-guard, dist-parity, mcp-close-task, mcp-append-comment-uat-guard) 74 passed ⬛ task-store-close-guards + uat-verdict-marker-compat 19 passed ⬛ `npm run test:all` 177 files/2037 passed. All green.

## MEDIUM discharged — the R3 checklist DID exist

The reviewer reviews cold and my relay omitted the five per-item outcomes, so it logged the gap (same as round 2) and asked the Orchestrator to confirm. **Confirming from the hand-off, all five stated:** (1) unspecced path exercised — ran `checkUatGuard`/`hasRecordedUatVerdict` through the full suite plus ad-hoc probes (clean step with no overall line; zero-width-space-prefixed overall line), both correctly false; (2) E1/E2 red-green planted via `git stash` of only the implementation files, verbatim output captured; (3) dist rebuilt via `npm run build:plugin`, only the two bundles changed, parity green; (4) parity copies n/a — no agent/skill files touched; (5) calibration n/a — no marker-carrying text carried forward. **Process note for future rounds: relay the checklist verbatim.** It cost a MEDIUM twice on this ticket.

## LOW carried forward

1. `src/close-guard.js:173` — optional `result` widens past the documented form, and the `Overall: PASS` accept branch has no committed positive lock. Fold into TASK-196's grammar doc-lock.
2. `src/close-guard.js:296-299` — in the no-step fallback (reachable only for ≤1-AC tickets) the "step block" is the entire body; one sentence in the residual doc would prevent misreading. Not a structural exemption — the fallback block is held to every strict rule.
3. `src/task-store.js:435-436` — widened `OVERALL_FAIL_RE` matches bare prose like "no overall failures were observed"; fail-closed friction, zero corpus hits. Deliberate, documented tradeoff.

## Blocking consequence for TASK-196 — read before scoping it

Independently confirmed twice: **0 of 45 historical uat comments satisfy the marker**, and a correctly-following orchestrator **cannot produce an accepted comment from today's documented convention** — `SKILL.md:452-455` never mandates the `Verdict:` label. The accepted grammar accumulated four undocumented requirements across these rounds: mandatory `Verdict:` label, no preamble at all, step count ≥ AC count, and a strict overall line. This is fail-CLOSED (it denies rather than admits), which is the only reason it was tolerable to defer — but the documented process is currently wrong. TASK-196's doc-lock must derive the **full accepted grammar from the guard**, not just the label.
